data.hypothesis: Measured (32,8,1) and (32,16,1) mappings were similarly fastest, while smaller Y extents were slower, but those results do not establish whether grouping work across Z within a CTA helps. This candidate uses (32,8,2): it retains adjacent-X warps at fixed Y/Z and 16 warps per CTA, while grouping two Z planes with eight Y rows. That may alter scheduling or cache behavior; it may also increase resource pressure. No speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Direct-global stencil mappings on this target; single-run samples are not confirmation.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured (32,8,1) and (32,16,1) candidates averaged about 3.474 µs, compared with 3.582 µs for baseline; several smaller Y extents were slower. These samples do not isolate the cause or establish repeatability.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this distinct Y/Z CTA grouping with the official full-run protocol, then compare repeated timings and correctness to the baseline.

data.notes: The launch now covers all 64×64×64 outputs with (32,8,2) threads and a ceil-divided grid. The controller must check signed varying inputs, independent endpoint values, correctness, and official timings; no new measurement or confirmation is claimed.
transformations: Change the one-output-per-thread kernel to compute Z as blockIdx.z * blockDim.z + threadIdx.z, with an output-boundary guard.
Use block (32,8,2) and a ceil-divided grid so every warp still spans adjacent X outputs at a fixed Y and Z, while grouping two Z planes in each CTA.
Retain direct global loads, all eight stencil neighbors and supplied coefficients, and the exact add-63/subtract-63 boundary correction, preserving in-range index 63.
